subject: Urgent: Rivermark nightly batch — throughput collapse and 500s
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@rivermark.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Rivermark Ops <ops@rivermark.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 02:15:00 -0700
Subject: [Rivermark] Nightly reconciliation batch causing 500s and throughput collapse

Avery —

We started seeing a degradation in the nightly reconciliation job at ~01:30 PDT this morning. The job that normally processes ~12k requests/minute dropped to ~2k/min and we're seeing a spike of 500 errors returned from the Redwood endpoint. p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~2.4s during the window. This is blocking our settlement process.

Key facts: 
- Window: 01:30–03:15 PDT
- Affected route: POST /v1/generate (private/vpc deployment)
- Sample request IDs: rmk-req-1134, rmk-req-1167, rmk-req-1199
- We're on private deployment (VPC) in us-west-2, model pinned to rw-infer/gpt-lite-v3 (customer-managed variant)

Attached: rivermark_batch_timeline.csv (timestamps + request ids), small snippet of errors.

We need immediate help — can you triage? We can open a 30-minute window to restart workers if that will help.

Sara
Sara Liu
SRE Lead, Rivermark Financial

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@rivermark.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 03:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Rivermark] Nightly reconciliation batch causing 500s and throughput collapse

Sara — thanks for the signal and the timeline. We're treating this as an incident. Looping Marissa (CS) and Evelyn (SRE) to coordinate.

Immediate asks from our side so we can triage quickly:
- Can you share the nginx/api gateway logs for the 01:20–03:30 window (we only need headers + upstream status)
- Confirm whether you have prefix/KV cache enabled and the last cache warm time before 01:30
- Which model variant is pinned (exact artifact hash) and whether you have an automatic fallback configured

Short-term mitigations we may try:
- Temporarily enable burst capacity on your VPC pool (adds 2x capacity for 10 minutes)
- Reduce max_batch_size and decrease batch timeout to lower P99 decode times
- Fallback to 1.2B quantized variant for the nightly job if decode CPU is the blocker

Can you confirm if you can do a controlled restart of the workers at 04:00 PDT? We can be on a 30-minute call at 03:30–04:00 to coordinate.

I'll start a forensic run on logs and share an internal playbook link as soon as we have log extracts.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Customer Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@rivermark.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 04:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Rivermark] Nightly reconciliation batch causing 500s and throughput collapse

Thanks for looping me in — quick read of the first log extracts Sara sent (attached as rmk_log_extract.txt) shows two concurrent symptoms we see often with private clusters: upstream 502/504s at the gateway while the model worker CPU saturates and the decode queue grows. Snippet from their gateway: 

  2027-06-01T01:37:42Z "POST /v1/generate" 502 upstream_timeout rw-worker-12
  2027-06-01T01:38:05Z "POST /v1/generate" 200 t=2.41s req=rmk-req-1167
  2027-06-01T01:39:01Z "POST /v1/generate" 503 upstream_overload rw-worker-7

Proposed immediate play (can execute in next 30–45m):
1) Toggle burst capacity on the VPC pool (adds ephemeral workers) — low risk.
2) On the deployment: decrease max_batch_size to 4 and batch_timeout_ms to 12ms for the nightly route. That reduces per-request latency for spiky workloads.
3) If (1)+(2) not sufficient, switch the job to the quantized fallback variant (rw-infer/gpt-lite-v3-1.2B-quant) for the 01:30–05:00 window.

I've attached our internal playbook excerpt (redwood_playbook_toggle.pdf) with exact CLI commands and an rsync-safe restart sequence. I'll also paste the playbook anchor below: 
https://redwood.internal/wiki/playbooks/private-throughput

If Sara confirms a maintenance window at 04:00, we can do (1)+(2) without impacting production batch outside the window.

—Marissa
Principal Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@rivermark.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 05:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Rivermark] Nightly reconciliation batch causing 500s and throughput collapse

Thanks — we can open a maintenance window and coordinate a worker restart at 04:00 PDT. Attaching our job config (rivermark_job_config.yaml).

Two notes from our side: 
- We have prefix caching enabled but it was last warmed at 23:00 yesterday (so cold start for some prefixes is expected).
- We can accept a fallback to the 1.2B quantized variant for the nightly job as a risk-mitigated path. Please proceed with the plan you outlined; we just ask for a short post-mortem and any recommended long-term config changes.

Appreciate the quick triage.

Sara

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@rivermark.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Rivermark] Nightly reconciliation batch causing 500s and throughput collapse

Quick exec summary and ask (for Monica and internal tracking):
- Incident: Rivermark private deployment experienced large throughput degradation and 500/502 responses during their nightly reconciliation job (01:30–03:15 PDT). Root cause appears to be decode queue saturation combined with cold prefix cache for a very bursty job.
- Immediate mitigation executed: Enabled burst capacity, reduced max_batch_size to 4 and batch_timeout_ms to 12ms for the nightly route, and applied fallback to 1.2B quantized variant for the 01:30–05:00 window. Customer restarted workers at 04:00; job completed with acceptable SLA (~95% success, p95 ~430ms).
- Follow-ups:
  1) Post-mortem (Marissa/Evelyn) due EOD tomorrow with exact timings and recommended config defaults for VPC-managed nightly jobs.
  2) Engineering consult: consider adding an automated temporary fallback when decode queue length > threshold.
  3) Commercial: customer asked for a credit for the 3-hour disruption — recommend we offer a one-time credit (suggest $10k) and a 30-day monitoring window.

Marissa/Evelyn — please file the internal incident, link logs and playbook, and I'll start the commercial thread with Monica. Sara — thanks for coordinating the restart and the job config; we'll follow up with the post-mortem and recommended config changes.

—Avery
